entry.title: Inside Pi: The Agent Wrapper
entry.summary: The first post in this series was about the agent loop, and one thing I liked about it was that it keeps no state between runs. You hand it a conversation, it works, it returns. But a coding agent has to remember things: the conversation so far, the messages you typed while it was busy, and whether you pressed Escape. entry.title: Inside Pi: The Agent Loop
entry.summary: Pi is a small, hackable coding agent that runs in your terminal. You give it a task, it talks to an LLM, and the LLM uses tools like “read this file” or “run this command” until the task is done.
